title: Golden Master Contract v1
description: WBS-40.01. A domain contract layered ON the shared outcome-contract-v1, never a second lifecycle: this record names no state, history, receipts or decision of its own. outcome_contract_ref points at the real outcome-contract-v1 JSON that owns those (state machine, receipts, history); scripts/golden_master_contract.py enforces that the referenced file exists and actually validates as outcome-contract-v1 before this record is accepted, so a golden-master contract can never point at nothing or at something malformed. Generic entity-resolution / MDM contract only: entity_type, examples, and every other field here name entity classes (customer/location, product/SKU, outlet, supplier) and general Golden Master mechanics, never a named client's own data, systems, or secrets. Only the keyword subset scripts/golden_master_contract.py actually enforces is used here: type, required, properties, enum, const, items, minItems, additionalProperties -- the same enforced subset outcome-contract-v1 and mobile-journey-contract-v1 document, for the same reason (a reader of any of the three files finds the same account).

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

master_id.description: A stable identifier for this one bounded golden-master record.

outcome_contract_ref.description: Path to the outcome-contract-v1 record this golden-master contract is layered on. Must resolve to a file that exists and validates as outcome-contract-v1 (enforced by hand, since the keyword subset has no cross-file reference check, matching how outcome_contract_ref is enforced by hand in mobile-journey-contract-v1).

entity_type.description: The class of entity this master record resolves, e.g. customer/location, product/SKU, outlet, or supplier (the roadmap's own examples, stated as examples rather than a closed list). Left as an open string rather than a closed enum: WBS-40 must materially help enterprise Golden Master work in general, and a fixed enum would refuse every entity type the roadmap did not happen to name.

business_purpose.description: Why this master record exists, in plain words: the business decision or process it serves, not an implementation description.

source_systems.description: The systems this master record is built from. At least one: a golden-master contract naming zero source systems describes no real master record.

downstream_consumers.description: Systems or processes that consume this master record downstream. May be empty for a master record not yet wired to a consumer.

critical_attributes.description: The attributes this master record is matched and merged on. At least one: a golden-master contract with no critical attributes has nothing to resolve entities against.

cardinality_constraints.description: Named cardinality rules this master record must hold (e.g. one customer maps to many locations). May be empty for an entity type with no stated constraint yet.

false_merge_cost_class.description: The cost class of wrongly merging two distinct real-world entities into one master record, stated in plain words (this schema does not fix the taxonomy's values, so a project's own review policy can name its own tiers).

missed_match_cost_class.description: The cost class of failing to merge two records that are the same real-world entity, stated in plain words (same open taxonomy as false_merge_cost_class).

review_policy.description: The human review policy this master record's merge decisions follow, in plain words (e.g. when a match is auto-merged versus routed to a human).

merge_threshold.description: The match score at or above which two candidate records are merged automatically.

review_threshold.description: The match score at or above which a candidate pair is routed to human review rather than discarded outright.

survivorship_policy_ref.description: A reference to where this master record's survivorship rules (which source wins per attribute) are defined. Not cross-file validated the way outcome_contract_ref is: this is a plain reference, not a second lifecycle record.

rollback_required.description: Whether this master record must carry a rollback path before it can publish merged results.

quality_claim_ids.description: Claim IDs this master record will feed once published (match precision, match recall, survivorship correctness, and similar). This contract does not score them itself. May be empty before publish.

locale_profiles.description: The locale profiles this master record's normalization must support (WBS-40.03's own concept: each normalization transform records the locale profile it ran under). At least one.

publish_authority.description: Who or what holds authority to publish this master record's merged results downstream.
